method: One GET /log.txt (9,703,824 bytes / ~78,500 lines, spanning 6 retained boots from 2026-05-07T15:07:45 to now) parsed with a Python regex census. Two extractions were run and reconciled: (A) the xochitl padded-column format, and (B) the 'category: msg' format used by every other daemon. Padding collisions were collapsed using the source-file path each line carries. No device state was read or changed.
volatility_warning: EVERY per-category line count in this file is a property of the rolling ~50 MB journal window at the moment of the fetch, NOT a firmware constant. journald.conf sets SystemMaxUse=50M with 47.5M already in use, so the oldest boots rotate out continuously. Several categories emit a fixed number of lines PER xochitl START (e.g. xofm.core.launcher, rm.library.loader, rm.user.auth.cli, rm.crashuploader.helpers all emit N-per-boot), so their counts move in lockstep with how many boots the window happens to retain. Cite counts as observations with a timestamp; never as a spec constant. The category NAMES, source files, and message shapes ARE stable.

log_format.format_C_no_pid: <iso8601-microsecond> <host> <ident>: <message> -- kernel: and the sleep-*.sh hook scripts carry NO [pid] and NO category; kernel lines alone are ~54% of the file
log_format.format_D_separators: -- Boot <boot-id> -- lines, bare, no host or ident
log_format.field_width_proof: The category field is exactly 25 columns wide, measured at the boundary: rm.epaperkeyboardhandler is 24 chars and is followed by 1 space (field=25); rm.network.authentication is 25 chars and is followed by ZERO spaces, so the message abuts the name with no separator. Also measured: rm.batterymanager len=17 pad=8, default len=7 pad=18, rm.search.indexsettings len=23 pad=2, rm.mdm.dbus-adaptor len=19 pad=6 -- every one sums to exactly 25.
log_format.field_width_evidence: $ python3 -c "re.search(r'xochitl\[\d+\]: \d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d\d\d (<cat>)( *)', raw)" over log5.txt -> "rm.epaperkeyboardhandler len= 24 pad=  1 field=25 / rm.network.authentication len= 25 pad=  0 field=25 / rm.batterymanager len= 17 pad=  8 field=25 / default len=  7 pad= 18 field=25 / rm.search.indexsettings len= 23 pad=  2 field=25 / rm.mdm.dbus-adaptor len= 19 pad=  6 field=25".
log_format.parsing_rule: A category name of 25 or more characters RUNS INTO its message with no separator, producing phantom category names. Split on the 25-column boundary, or resolve against the known name set. A whitespace-splitting parser reports 57 raw tokens for what are actually 47 categories in format A.

census.evidence: $ python3 <census script> over log5.txt -> "RAW padded tokens: 57 / colon-format names: 10 / distinct rm.*/xofm.* after collapse: 49 / non-rm/xofm categories: {'default': 155, 'qt.network.http2': 152}".
census.collision_evidence: $ python3 <census script> COLLISION MAP output -> "rm.entryfile.documentcontentfileLock -> rm.entryfile.documentcontentfile / rm.epaperevdevtouchscreenhandler{evdevtouch,pmax,pmin,rotate,screenGeometry,xmax,xmin,ymax,ymin} -> rm.epaperevdevtouchscreenhandler / rm.network.authentication{Fetching,User,userTokenHostname} -> rm.network.authentication"; the remaining six were resolved by their source-file path, which is unambiguous (e.g. rm.batterymanager.slumberinhibitorerased carries .../batterymanager/src/slumberinhibitor.cpp and the message 'erased N invalid slumber inhibitors').

not_a_category.rm.tmp: matches 255 times in the log but is NOT a logger category: 0 occurrences in the category column. All hits are the '.rm.tmp' FILE SUFFIX inside rm.scenefile's 'Scene written to:' messages. A naive \b(rm|xofm)\.\w+ regex over the whole line invents it.
not_a_category.rm.library: Bare rm.library is NOT present in this window. $ grep -oE ' rm\.library[a-z.]*' log5.txt | sort | uniq -c -> only rm.library.ext.open, rm.library.loader, rm.library.view. A prior session recorded one bare rm.library line ('Trying to create collection with invalid parent, defaulting to toplevel') dated 2026-04-29, which has since rotated out -- which is why this window reports 49 categories where an earlier one reported 50.

claims.governs: The USB web server's request ROUTER. This IS the oracle for the HTTP surface.
claims.shape: Exactly TWO message shapes: 'Bad path "<path>" "<second>"' (second arg empty in 100% of 59 distinct occurrences) and 'ERROR "<message>"'. No source path is ever logged. Nine known ERROR strings: Unknown file, Malformed URL, No file sent, Filetype not supported, Unable to open file /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets, Missing thumbnail ID, Unable to get thumbnail for entry, Can only download documents, No such entry.
claims.evidence: $ python3 <shape census> for rm.usb.web -> "174 lines, 70 shapes" with the top shapes "71 ERROR \"Unknown file\" / 18 ERROR \"Filetype not supported\" / 5 ERROR \"Malformed URL\" / 4 Bad path \"/documents\" \"\" / 3 ERROR \"Unable to open file /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets\" / 2 ERROR \"No file sent\"" (the 70 shapes are 59 distinct Bad path values plus the error strings).
claims.verdict_semantics: Not-routed = the PAIR (Bad path, then ERROR "Unknown file"). Routed-but-rejected = a BARE ERROR line with no preceding Bad path. Routed-and-succeeded = NO line at all. See http.json claim oracle:verdict-pairs for the bracketed-sentinel technique.
claims.notes: Static assets are served from /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets. '/documents' without a trailing slash is a Bad path while '/documents/' is valid -- the trailing slash is load-bearing. Since xochitl owns no D-Bus name, this category is the ONLY window into the HTTP server, and its verbosity is not bus-tunable.

claims.governs: The cloud sync engine's run loop, in the rm-sync PROCESS (format B: 'rm-sync[486]: rm.synchronizer: <msg>'). Loudest category by a factor of 1.6.
claims.shape: Scheduling ('-- execute requested: <ISO8601>', '-- execute ended: <ISO8601>'), batching ('-- running sync, batch: N/-1, minimal:true|false' and 'batch: N/1'), and per-document eligibility ('document <uuid> has failure, not locking'). No source path logged.
claims.evidence: $ python3 <shape census> for rm.synchronizer -> "2592 lines, 137 shapes" with "1956 document <uuid> has failure, not locking / 163 -- execute ended: N-N-NTN:N:N.N / 148 -- execute requested: N-N-NTN:N:N.N / 113 -- running sync, batch: N/-N, minimal:true / 33 -- running sync, batch: N/-N, minimal:false / 15 -- running sync, batch: N/N, minimal:true".
claims.notes: This is the authoritative verdict on .failure: the synchronizer reads the marker, declines the document lock, and therefore never enters the document in .tree. 1956 of its 2592 lines are that one message, over exactly the 12 .failure UUIDs. Companion category rm.documentlockmanager is the lock side of the same mechanism. Also emits 'Stopping sync because of network-level failure' and 'sync resolution: root hash (local=... server=...)'.

claims.governs: The per-document worker thread: one spawned and retired per open document UUID, and the thing that loads page stroke data.
claims.shape: Five messages: '-> worker on <uuid> now running', '-> worker on <uuid> now exiting (run ...:1603 or :1487)', 'loaded pageId=<uuid>, version=6 (loadLinesForPageUnprotected ...)', 'loaded pageId=<uuid> - no file found (loadLinesForPageUnprotected ...)', 'no renderer possible for file type: ' (trailing empty type).
claims.evidence: $ python3 <census> -> "1397  rm.docworker   src/worker/src/documentworker.cpp"; per-shape breakdown from a bracketed sample: "859 loaded pageId=<uuid> - no file found / 18 loaded pageId=<uuid>, version=6 / 11 -> worker on <uuid> now running / 9 -> worker on <uuid> now exiting / 8 no renderer possible for file type: ".
claims.notes: The most valuable category for a client parsing .rm. 'version=6' confirms the v6 format per page. '- no file found' marks a page entry with no .rm on disk -- and it is the OVERWHELMING majority (95% in the sampled window), which is the device's own statement that .rm is per-page optional. loadLinesForPageUnprotected emits from three different line numbers (2400, 2402, 2330), so no single line number is a stable signature. 'no renderer possible for file type: ' with an EMPTY type corresponds to the zero-byte .rm placeholders in the .failure documents.

claims.governs: xochitl's internal NAMED-TIMER framework. Every firing is logged with the timer's name, making it a free schedule map of the application.
claims.shape: 'Type::{Normal|Rtc} timer <name> timed out (operator() .../timer.cpp:27)'. Type:: is a two-valued ENUM, not a literal, and Rtc is the MAJORITY.

timer_names.Rtc sleepDelayTimer: the loudest single timer, ~49% of the category

There is no rm.sys.timer unit; only 4 timers are loaded device-wide and the reMarkable one is rm-sanity.timer. The RTC half of this category is the power/sleep scheduling and is the half a client actually wants.

claims.governs: Serialization of the CRDT scene (.rm) file.
claims.shape: Three shapes, and the TYPO MATTERS: 'Scene written to: "<path>.rm.tmp"' (226), 'Scene writen to: "<path>.rm.tmp"' (29, sic), 'File has UUID map with N entries' (67). No source path logged.
claims.evidence: $ python3 <shape census> for rm.scenefile -> "322 lines, 3 shapes / 226  Scene written to: \"/home/root/.local/share/remarkable/xochitl/<uuid>/<uuid>.rm.tmp\" / 67  File has UUID map with N entries / 29  Scene writen to: \"...<uuid>.rm.tmp\"".
parser_requirements: Writes go to a .rm.TMP sibling first and are then renamed, so polling a .rm during active editing can catch a half-written or absent file.
The firmware ships BOTH spellings, 'writen' and 'written' -- the typo was fixed mid-history and both are live in one journal window. String-matching this line needs both.
'File has UUID map with N entries' is the CRDT author/UUID table the v6 format carries.

claims.governs: The e-paper TOUCH (finger) input handler over evdev. Produces NINE phantom names on a naive parse (32-char category).

hard_device_facts.device: /dev/input/event3, name "Elan touch input", discovered via device discovery
hard_device_facts.pressure: min 0, max 0 -- touch reports NO pressure

claims.evidence: $ grep -a 'rm.epaperevdevtouchscreenhandler' log5.txt | sed 's/^.*rm\.epaperevdevtouchscreenhandler//' | sort -u -> "evdevtouch: /dev/input/event3 / evdevtouch: /dev/input/event3: device name: Elan touch input / evdevtouch: /dev/input/event3: min pressure: 0 max pressure: 0 / evdevtouch: /dev/input/event3: min X: 0 max X: 2064 / evdevtouch: /dev/input/event3: min Y: 0 max Y: 2832 / evdevtouch: Adding device at /dev/input/event3 / evdevtouch: Updating QInputDeviceManager device count: 1 touch devices, 0 pending handler(s) / evdevtouch: Using device /dev/input/event3 / evdevtouch: Using device discovery / pmax 0 / pmin 0 / rotate QTransform(type=TxNone, 11=1 12=0 13=0 21=0 22=1 23=0 31=0 32=0 33=1) / screenGeometry QRect(0,0 1620x2160) / xmax 2064 / xmin 0 / ymax 2832 / ymin 0".
claims.consequence: Touch reports min pressure == max pressure == 0, so pressure in .rm strokes comes ONLY from the pen digitizer, never from touch. And the 2064x2832 touch grid is a DIFFERENT coordinate space from the 1620x2160 display, so raw touch coordinates need scaling.

Token expiry: <timestamp>".

Measured: every printed fragment is exactly 23 chars long and identical across all occurrences. No key material and no signature is printed, so these lines are safe -- but a client should still not echo them verbatim.

claims.governs: The OUTBOUND (client-side) HTTP transaction lifecycle -- the reMarkable-to-cloud direction. NOT to be confused with rm.usb.web, which is the inbound server.
claims.shape: "Request failed: RequestId=<n> error='<qt error>' http=none url=<url>" (finish, :319), "Request failed: RequestId=<n> http=optional(400 Bad request) url=<url>", and "RequestId=<n>: transaction ended in <N>ms after following events:" (:114) followed by indented Create/Send/Fail continuation lines.

claims.critical_bias: This category ONLY logs FAILURES. Grepping it yields a 100%-failure sample whether or not the cloud works. Do NOT infer 'cloud unreachable' from it. Outcome-logging siblings show the same endpoints succeeding: rm.synchronizer 'sync resolution: root hash (... server=Hash(...))' requires a successful authenticated cloud GET, rm.network.notifications logs 'Connected to notifications server', and rm.updates.betaprogram logs 'Request finished' 62 times against 4 network errors.

The wrapped continuation lines are the source of the '(~Transaction' and empty-field extraction artifacts.

claims.governs: The INBOUND HTTP listener's BIND step -- the sibling of rm.usb.web one layer down.
claims.shape: 'No valid hostaddress found'. No source path logged.

The same HttpListener component logs its bind SUCCESS under category `default`, not rm.httplistener: "xochitl[416]: 15:01:46.423 default   HttpListener: Listening on port 80". On the CURRENT boot rm.httplistener has ZERO occurrences and only the `default` success line is present; the 3 retained failures are from older-firmware boots. claims.governs: The persistent push/notification SOCKET to the cloud and its reconnect supervision -- distinct from the request/response rm.http.* path.
claims.shape: 'Connected to notifications server (onStateChanged ...:220)', 'Notifications socket is OK: ConnectedState (checkIfShouldConnect ...:270)', '... ConnectingState'. Build cutover at 2026-05-09T18:40 shifted onStateChanged :210 -> :220 and checkIfShouldConnect :260 -> :270.
claims.evidence: $ python3 <census> -> "113  rm.network.notifications  src/notifications/src/notifications.cpp"; per-shape from a sample: "60 Connected to notifications server (onStateChanged .../notifications.cpp:220) / 34 Notifications socket is OK: ConnectingState (checkIfShouldConnect .../notifications.cpp:270) / 6 ...:260 / 6 Notifications socket is OK: ConnectedState (...:270) / 6 Connected to notifications server (...:210)".
claims.caveats: ConnectedState/ConnectingState are generic QAbstractSocket state names shared by QTcpSocket, QSslSocket and QLocalSocket, and NO host, port, scheme or URL appears in any of the 113 lines -- so this category alone does not prove the channel is a cloud WebSocket. It also is not one long-lived connection: 15 separate 'Connected to notifications server' events occurred in a ~7-hour span, and the supervising function is named checkIfShouldConnect, i.e. it POLLS the socket's own state.

claims.governs: Write-locking a document while it is open, plus the sleep-to-upload handoff.
claims.shape: Exactly two messages: 'Opening document in unlocked mode: <uuid> (setDocument ...:54)' and 'Going to sleep, trigger upload timeout for doc <uuid> (setSleepState ...:99)'.

refuted.correction: Line counts are rolling-window observations, not spec constants. Several categories emit a FIXED number of lines PER BOOT (xofm.core.launcher 1, rm.crashuploader.helpers 1, rm.library.loader 1, rm.user.auth.cli 1, rm.epaperkeyboardhandler 4, xofm.modules.search 2), so their counts move in lockstep with retained boots and can never be stable. Some of the original figures were also cross-contaminated between adjacent categories (28 was rm.modules.mdm.dbus.policyagent's count, not rm.modules.mdm.policymanager's). Cite counts with a timestamp; cite names, sources and message shapes as the durable facts.

refuted.claim: rm.sys.timer message form is 'Type::Normal timer <name> timed out', with four timer names: entryUploadTimer, markerSleepDebounceTimer, calendarUpdateTimer, jsonReporter.
refuted.observation: Type:: is a two-valued ENUM, not the literal 'Normal', and Type::Rtc is the MAJORITY (542 of 874 in a measured sample, 62%). Nine distinct timer names exist, not four, and the loudest single timer -- Type::Rtc sleepDelayTimer at 428 lines, 49% of the whole category -- is absent from the list, along with lockUploadTimer, lightSleepTimer, searchIndexEnableTimer and mcuFirmwareUpdateTimer.
refuted.correction: 'Type::{Normal|Rtc} timer <name> timed out (operator() .../timer.cpp:27)'. The RTC half is the power/sleep scheduling, i.e. the half a client actually needs. Source file and line 27 and 'third-loudest' all verified.

refuted.claim: rm.light.front's 'Turning off lights' is a reliable sleep marker -- the cheapest awake/asleep signal in the log after rm.batterymanager.
refuted.observation: It is not. After the last 'Turning off lights' at 22:08:30, with no intervening light-on line, the device accepted two SSH logins, spun up three HTTP connection handler threads, and served the /log.txt fetch itself through 22:09:05 -- 35 seconds later. rm.batterymanager.suspenddelay logged 'PowerStateRm12x requests a delay of 24740ms' at 22:08:42, i.e. suspend was still explicitly deferred. The event is an idle-timer step: on-to-off deltas measured 19:00 exactly, four times.
refuted.correction: It marks the START of a ~19-minute idle light-sleep sequence, not the moment the device becomes unreachable. And the bare string is ambiguous: rm.light.keyboard emits the identical text ~1 ms later, so the string double-counts. For 'is it about to sleep', prefer login1's PrepareForSleep(b) signal, or rm.batterymanager.suspenddelay.

refuted.claim: rm.stp.impl is the consumer half of a live pipeline whose fetcher half is rm.libs.integrations, and it governs Dropbox / Google Drive / OneDrive class integrations.
refuted.observation: It is a dead PREDECESSOR, renamed across firmware. Its last line is 2026-05-09T18:40:21; the identical message resumes 43 seconds later under rm.libs.integrations from a different source file, under a NEW pid, and runs for 3.5 months. ZERO pid overlap: no xochitl process ever emits both. Two halves of one pipeline would co-emit in-process. src/syncthirdparty/src/impl.cpp:75 is the ONLY syncthirdparty emit site in 9.7 MB, and a live subsystem would have more than one. Provider attribution has no support: 'dropbox', 'google drive', 'gdrive', 'onedrive' all have zero hits.
refuted.correction: See claim rm.stp.impl. Only 'zero integrations configured' survives.

refuted.claim: rm.httplistener's only logged message is the bind failure, and it is what you would see if the usb gadget interface has not come up.
refuted.observation: A category-scoped grep is BLIND to the success path, which the same component logs under category `default`: 'HttpListener: Listening on port 80'. On the current boot rm.httplistener has ZERO occurrences and only the default success line is present; the 3 retained failures are older-firmware boots. The gadget theory also fails: systemd-networkd logged usb0 and usb1 'Link UP' ~3.7 seconds BEFORE every one of those failures, and usb-ether-once reported 'usbnet ready' on all 6 boots including the 3 that failed.
refuted.correction: See claim rm.httplistener. The weaker true statement is that the few retained lines happen to be bind failures on older firmware.

refuted.claim: rm.filesystem: 5 lines, two message forms, every one a missing .pagedata -- which proves the firmware tolerates a missing .pagedata.
refuted.observation: THREE message forms, not two: the third is '... failed: "file to open is a directory"'. Only 4 of 5 lines in the cited sample concerned .pagedata; the 5th was /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets, i.e. the HTTP static handler, making this a GENERIC failed-open channel with two errno classes. Only 2 of the 5 carried the file-system.cpp:67 suffix -- the raw open() lines carry no source location at all. And the tolerance conclusion is unsupported by these lines: no success path is logged, so nothing here distinguishes tolerated-absence from unnoticed-absence.
refuted.correction: See claim rm.filesystem. The .pagedata-is-optional conclusion is true, but it is established by the .metadata/.content census (2 of 42), not by this category.

refuted.claim: xofm.modules.search is the strongest evidence that the one .db in the data dir is a search index, and 'RetrievalIntent::GenerationNotLoaded' plus a 'Generation' concept implies handwriting-recognition-backed retrieval.
refuted.observation: The two lines are construction-time only and name no file. 'rm-search-index' has ZERO hits in the whole log; the only '.db' strings anywhere are the logger category names rm.mdm.db and rm.modules.mdm.db; and 'handwrit|myscript|text recognition' has zero hits. The evidence holds identically whether the subsystem indexes anything or not.
refuted.correction: The filename rm-search-index.db in the directory listing establishes that, plus the on-device FTS5 schema read (see filesystem.json). This category establishes only that xochitl constructs a SqliteSearchSystem per start and flips an IndexSettings flag.

refuted.claim: rm.user.module ties the software stack to hardware state: because secboot='unlocked' the pkcs11 signer is unavailable and the device falls back to 'none'. The firmware states the causal link itself. Explains why pcscd.service is disabled while pcscd.socket listens.
refuted.observation: The firmware states no such link. 'secboot' and 'secure boot' have ZERO hits in the log, and so does 'pcscd'. The hardware story is contradicted: keystore.service successfully initialises OP-TEE PKCS11 device- and user-tokens 3.9 seconds earlier in the same boot, so the secure-element signer exists. The only other producer of 'unlocked' is mdm-agent reading MDM device state from sysfs.
refuted.correction: The weaker supportable statement: xochitl's userauth setup logs once per start that it fell back to signing mechanism 'none' after seeing an 'unlocked' state whose referent it never names. The provider actually in use is OP-TEE, not PC/SC. Also the message ends '(signingMechanism <path>:39)' with a line number, not '[signingMechanism]'.

refuted.claim: rm.documentlockmanager shows that a document's sync only STARTS after the device sleeps.
refuted.observation: Contradicted. On one measured day 12 rm.synchronizer 'running sync' events (14:58:19 through 17:23:29) preceded the day's first sleep-to-upload event at 17:42:32. Additionally xochitl DOES use a real lock file elsewhere, 'Lock path="/tmp/library-enumeration.lock"', so 'the lock is advisory, not a flock' is unestablished as a general statement.
refuted.correction: Sleep triggers an upload TIMEOUT, and only the 'batch: N/1' synchronizer runs cluster after sleep. Both message strings, both line numbers (54, 99) and the source file verified exact.

refuted.claim: rm.http.backend is logged twice per process start, so its line count is effectively a process-restart counter.
refuted.observation: Per-pid emission is 2, 4 or 8 lines -- the backend is constructed 1-4 times per process. A 44-line sample maps to 10 distinct pids, and pids recur across boots.
refuted.correction: The pair fires once per BACKEND CONSTRUCTION, not once per process start. Line count is not a restart counter. Source file, both messages and the dual Qt/curl finding all verified; line numbers are :31/:67 on current firmware, :27/:63 on the older boots.

refuted.claim: rm.light.keyboard's presence proves a Type Folio is attached to this device.
refuted.observation: It does not. The category emits at byte-identical timestamps to rm.light.front on every sleep/wake -- an unconditional module hook, not a hardware probe. It fired on 26 distinct days in the window while 'folio' appears on only 5, and the log contains no HID or physical-keyboard enumeration line at all. The only folio signal is the cover magnet (RM_HWMON_WS_FOLIO_OPENED / 'Woke up with reason=FolioOpen'), which any folio trips.
refuted.correction: It proves the back-light module is compiled in and hooked to sleep/wake. Source path is lowercase src/xofm/modules/light/back/setup.cpp; the category/directory naming mismatch is real and worth recording.

refuted.claim: Three non-rm/xofm logger categories share the column: qt.network.http2, default, and qml.
refuted.observation: Two. There is no qml category: the string 'qml' occurs in only 6 lines of the entire journal, every one inside a qrc:/qml/... resource path within a `default`-category QML engine error. A bare 'qml' token never lands in the category column.
refuted.correction: qt.network.http2 and default. The two extraction ARTIFACTS the claim also flagged (an empty field, and '(~Transaction' from transaction.cpp:114) are real and correctly identified as wrapped continuations.

refuted.claim: /log.txt is the live system journal byte-for-byte, start-aligned.
refuted.observation: It is a REDACTION-FILTERED rendering. 407 lines replace MAC, BSSID and SSID values with the literal string '<redacted>', versus 0 such lines in journalctl output, and in 223 of them the redaction SWALLOWS the rest of the line (e.g. journal 'bssid=<mac> reason=3 locally_generated=1' becomes 'bssid<redacted>ated=1'). Scope: 381 wpa_supplicant lines, 24 kernel configfs-gadget MAC lines, 2 iw61x lines. It also renders at microsecond precision, i.e. `-o short-iso-precise`, not `-o short-iso`.
refuted.correction: /log.txt is journal-DERIVED with a lossy wifi-identifier scrubber. Matched values are unrecoverable from it. The oracle itself is unaffected: 0 of the 174 rm.usb.web lines carry '<redacted>'. Also note /log.txt ships an undocumented header, Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="log-<request-time>.txt".

refuted.claim: The /log.txt parsing contract is two line formats: (A) xochitl padded, (B) other daemons 'category: msg'.
refuted.observation: Those two cover only ~44% of the file. 42,785 of ~78,500 lines (54%) are `kernel:` lines with NO [pid] and NO category; the sleep-*.sh hook scripts likewise have no [pid]; 296 xochitl lines carry no HH:MM:SS.mmm prefix at all (e.g. 'xochitl[406]: xofm.core.launcher: Running with args=["--system"]', 'xochitl[406]: debug: ...'); and '-- Boot <id> --' separators are bare.
refuted.correction: Four formats. See the log_format block at the top of this file.

refuted.observation: It depends entirely on whether the rm-sync process's format-B lines are counted. Within the xochitl padded format it is #1 (1600 vs rm.docworker 1397). Across all emitters rm.synchronizer is #1 at 2592, making rm.batterymanager #2.
refuted.correction: State the scope. #1 among xochitl-emitted categories; #2 device-wide behind rm.synchronizer. The source-file attribution (src/xofm/libs/batterymanager/src/batterymanager.cpp, 100% of lines) is exact.

refuted.claim: All cloud endpoint failures include https://eu.tectonic.remarkable.com/sync/v4/root at RequestId=102.
refuted.observation: Neither exists. 'sync/v4' has zero hits anywhere in the journal; the only sync URL emitted is sync/v3/files/{sha256-hex}, and the cited RequestId=102 does not exist (the real line is RequestId=49). The endpoint list also omitted search/v1/settings, which fails identically.
refuted.correction: Observed cloud URLs: eu.tectonic.remarkable.com/{discovery/v1/endpoints, settings/v1/beta, integrations/v2/instances, search/v1/settings, sync/v3/files/{sha256}} plus ping.remarkable.com/analytics/v2/events (standing 400) and the token host webapp-prod.cloud.remarkable.engineering. Separately, 'all cloud endpoints failing' is itself an artifact of rm.http.transaction's failure-only logging -- see that claim's critical_bias field.
